shouldFix.subjectText: 4 attacksNotChargedWithDisclosure objects D01, D02, D03, D04 (members id, observation, whyNotCharged) travel as honesty work
evidence: docs/coop/artifacts/g29-fixture-corpus.v2.review-independent.claude2.json (60bb9651a51a0d66f36613d68e8af232a7f402002082d92e5d75a41cd7207ce5, the digest this entry itself pins at line 65): jq '.attacksNotChargedWithDisclosure[] | keys' returns, in order, ["id","observation","suggestedIfALaterVersionIsAuthored","whyNotCharged"] for D01 and ["id","observation","whyNotCharged"] for D02, D03 and D04. The set is heterogeneous; the recited tuple is true of three of the four objects and short by one member for D01.

The omitted member is not empty boilerplate. D01.suggestedIfALaterVersionIsAuthored carries a concrete repair addressed to a future author: 'Write it as D-318-scoped past standing - D-318 left per-platform copies to a later successor; g29-fixture-corpus.v2 is that successor - matching the correction pattern predecessorV1.role and leftoverJoinV6.role already use.' That is precisely the class of content the disposition table exists to carry forward as honesty work.

The register treats '(members ...)' as an EXHAUSTIVE, byte-derived tuple, not an illustrative subset. Decisive instance, inside one sentence of the recorded D-335 entry: 'Claude Stage A g21-fixture-corpus.v16 returned 3 named advisories objects ... (members id, title, measurement, whyNotAFinding) and 6 named observations objects ... (members id, title, measurement)'. The two tuples differ by exactly one key, and the bytes of g21-fixture-corpus.v16.review-independent.claude2.json confirm it: all 3 advisories have keys id,measurement,title,whyNotAFinding and all 6 observations have keys id,measurement,title. A convention that draws a one-key distinction that finely cannot absorb a silently dropped fourth member here.

Nine distinct '(members ...)' tuples occur across the live COORD - including 4-member and 5-member forms and two orderings of the same 5 - and every one sampled reproduces its review's key list exactly. There is no recorded precedent for an under-inclusive tuple.

The register's own handling of a heterogeneous disclosure set in this very lineage avoided the problem rather than flattening it: COORD D-318, reciting the Claude Stage A review of g29-fixture-corpus.v1 whose two attacksNotChargedWithDisclosure objects are ["observation","suggestedIfALaterVersionIsAuthored","whyNotCharged"] and ["observation","whyNotCharged"], wrote '2 attacksNotChargedWithDisclosure objects with no id field' - a shape claim true of both objects - and stated no member tuple at all.

Grading rationale. This is the shape-measurement class of CLAUDE-D284-SF1 and of the D-320 turn-1 findings against this same lineage, where MF-1 (shape word 'strings' false of objects, and repeated in the operative Decision) took MUST-FIX while SF-1 (proposition true, citation imprecise, single site) took SHOULD-FIX. This defect sits at the SHOULD-FIX end of that pair: the count '4', the shape word 'objects', the four identifiers and the honesty-work standing are all byte-true; the three named members really are members; the defect is confined to one cell and is NOT repeated in the operative Decision paragraph, which at lines 138-140 recites '4 attacksNotChargedWithDisclosure objects D01, D02, D03, D04' with no member tuple. No gate, digest, count, authority claim or denial in the entry turns on it.

It is not cured elsewhere in the file: line 82 is the only site that recites the disclosure members, so no other binding site makes the reader whole (the test applied at CLAUDE-CMLJ-V12-A1 for demoting a dropped assertion to an advisory).

reviewSummary: Twenty-seven attacks run against the D-342 draft; twenty-six refuted, one sustained. The subject is unmoved at a95d99b5... mode 0444; HEAD, live COORD and file 08 are unmoved at the dispatch digests, and this review edited none of them. All six pinned digests recompute. The forty copies exist on disk under four platform directories, are byte-identical to the ten D-318 implementations at 40 of 40, and carry no Windows directory. The D-002 platform list is quoted, not invented: G10 occupancy v2 $.platforms is ordered-equal to G23 occupancy v2 and identical to the subject's recital, which is the only lawful route because G29 occupancy v3 has no platforms key. OQ-G29-2 is answered on the D-247 precedent. Leftover-design of OBL-G29-FX-AUTHORING is left open on leftover-join.v6 of G29 on three grounds that all check out; the staleness of the forty copies is expressly deferred; leftover-join.v4 of G29 is kept historical; nothing is marked SATISFIED; file 08 is untouched; required-now stays 28; every leftover-join token is lineage-qualified and no deictic self-naming appears. One defect survives. The Stage A disposition table recites an exhaustive member tuple '(members id, observation, whyNotCharged)' for the four Claude attacksNotChargedWithDisclosure objects, but D01 carries a fourth member, suggestedIfALaterVersionIsAuthored, holding a concrete repair for a later author. The register's '(members ...)' parenthetical is an exhaustive byte-derived tuple - D-335 draws a one-key distinction between two such tuples in a single sentence and the bytes confirm it - and D-318 handled this same lineage's heterogeneous disclosure set by stating a true-of-all fact instead. Graded SHOULD-FIX rather than MUST-FIX: the count, the shape word, the four identifiers and the honesty-work standing are all byte-true, the three named members really are members, the defect sits in one table cell and is not repeated in the operative Decision paragraph, and no gate, digest, count or denial turns on it. Under the dispatch rule, one surviving SHOULD-FIX forecloses CONSENT.
decision: OBJECT - 0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX (SF-1). Twenty-seven attacks run, twenty-six refuted, one sustained.
